prompt: Hey, I need the release notes in docs/release-notes.md converted to a CSV file. Please create docs/release-notes.csv with these columns: version, date, type, summary. Each bullet point should be a separate row. The type is the heading the bullet sits under (like 'New Features', 'Improvements', etc.). Let me know when it's done.

rubric.criterion: The CSV is cleanly formatted with proper quoting and no extraneous content. Fail: docs/release-notes.csv is missing, has the wrong header (not version, date, type, summary), or fields containing commas are unquoted so rows have the wrong number of columns. Partial: the header and quoting are right, but there are extra rows (headings or blank lines as rows) or notes text, or one bullet is split across rows. Pass: the header is exactly version,date,type,summary, each bullet is one row, any field with a comma or quote is quoted correctly, and the file holds no extra text.

Correctly handles the tricky cases in the source: a comma inside quoted text, a date in a different format, and wrapped lines. Fail: none of the three is handled, or a wrapped bullet becomes two rows. Partial: one or two of the three are handled, for example the comma is quoted but the odd date is copied in its own format, or the wrapped line is joined but the summary is cut. Pass: the quoted comma stays inside its summary field, every date appears in one consistent format (and the message says how the odd one was converted), and each wrapped bullet is joined into a single complete summary on one row.

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the date format chosen for the odd date and how wrapped bullets were joined stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/release-notes.csv was written. Partial: it names docs/release-notes.csv and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the date format chosen for the odd date and how wrapped bullets were joined. Pass: it names docs/release-notes.csv and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the date format chosen for the odd date and how wrapped bullets were joined still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

verdicts.note: Prompt only specifies what output is wanted (convert markdown to CSV with specific columns), not how to do it. No method, framework, or process is named.

Prompt clearly specifies input path (docs/release-notes.md), output path (docs/release-notes.csv), column names, and that each bullet is a row. The type mapping is explained. The main traps (date normalization, CSV quoting) are implicit in 'convert to CSV' - a reasonable agent would handle these.

Task requires handling specific edge cases (date normalization, proper CSV quoting for commas, multi-line bullets) that a quick/naive answer would miss. Hidden tests check for exact row counts (67 total, 12 for 6.2.0, etc.) and proper CSV formatting. A quick answer would lose significant points.
No scriptedUser or hidden facts. Task is straightforward conversion. Reference passes all 23 hidden tests. No impossible requirements.

No ASKS.json, no scriptedUser facts, no hints in fixture files. The solution/ directory contains reference output but an agent has no reason to discover or read it. Task-draft.json notes are for task authors only, not visible to agents.

items.note: The prompt asks to convert release notes to CSV with columns version, date, type, summary without naming any method or framework. No misleading hints or decoys.
The fixture contains docs/release-notes.md as source, but nothing in the fixture (comments, docs, tests, names) lists release-notes.csv or describes the finished CSV behavior.

The checks (file_exists, header, quoting, date 2024-01-28 for 6.1.3, 67 rows) and rubric (clean-conversion, handles-edge-cases, honest-summary) all match the fixture (docs/release-notes.md has all versions, bullets, special characters) and request (convert to CSV).

A developer can read docs/release-notes.md and create release-notes.csv per the prompt (version,date,type,summary columns, one row per bullet). The tricky cases (commas, date format, line wrapping) are deterministically deducible from the source.
